articles.title: A Pikachu Plush Spent 67 Days Aboard the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: The ESA–Pokémon partnership for World Space Week sent a spacesuited plush into orbit with astronaut Sophie Adenot; 1,040 orbits later, the tour video is out.
articles.image_caption: A Pikachu plush in a custom spacesuit floats inside the International Space Station's Cupola observatory. The toy spent 67 days aboard the station as part of an ESA-Pokémon partnership marking World Space Week.
articles.nri_angle: The ISS crew includes Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon on Expedition 75 — and ESA's Pikachu partnership shows how space agencies are reaching the next generation of young space fans, including in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manus Raises Over $500 Million in First Round Since Meta Breakup
articles.excerpt: Butterfly Effect's AI agent startup, unwound from Meta's $2 billion-plus acquisition by Beijing in April, now has fresh capital and a reported $500 million revenue run rate.
articles.image_caption: The Manus logo displayed on a screen. The AI agent startup raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since unwinding Meta's $2 billion-plus acquisition.
articles.nri_angle: The Manus raise signals accelerating commercial demand for AI agents — the same enterprise AI wave that India's IT services firms and 2,000+ global capability centres are racing to serve.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Scraps Landmark $5 Billion IPO, Blaming Market Volatility
articles.excerpt: The AI data-center builder withdrew its ASX listing — set to be Australia's biggest since Telstra — after investors balked at a $44 billion valuation; it will raise private capital instead.
articles.image_caption: Server racks and monitoring displays inside a data center. Firmus, which builds AI data centers, withdrew its landmark Australian listing on October 9, citing market volatility.
articles.nri_angle: A landmark AI-infrastructure IPO collapse that signals how selectively markets are now pricing the AI boom — relevant context for tech investors and professionals worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio's 1,600-Satellite Plan Gets Green Light as Starlink's India Launch Stalls
articles.excerpt: IN-SPACe has cleared Reliance Jio's low-Earth-orbit constellation as technically sound, while Starlink, JioSatcom and Eutelsat OneWeb await Home Ministry security clearances before switching on commercial services.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk appears in a graphic showing Starlink satellites over India. Starlink has secured a satcom licence and IN-SPACe authorisation, but commercial services await a pending Home Ministry security clearance.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in India's remote regions, Jio's sovereign constellation promises affordable rural broadband — and SpaceX-style competition could cut the cost of staying connected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Bans Russian and Iranian Networks Using ChatGPT for Influence Campaigns
articles.excerpt: The company says the Russian 'Dark Clark' operation was the most sophisticated front-identity campaign it has disrupted, while Iran's 'Bogus Bylines' placed nearly 100 articles in real outlets under fake journalist personas.
articles.image_caption: A silhouetted figure works at a bank of monitors in a dark operations room. OpenAI says Russian and Iranian operatives used ChatGPT to draft reports and content for covert influence campaigns targeting Latin America and other regions.
articles.nri_angle: One Russian front posed as a platform covering the Indian diaspora in Latin America — evidence that diaspora communities are prime targets for influence operations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Navya Naveli Nanda Launches Naveli Ventures to Back India's Deep-Tech Ambitions
articles.excerpt: The Nanda Family Office's venture arm will invest across deep-tech, space, AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and health — formalising a strategy three years in the making.
articles.image_caption: Navya Naveli Nanda photographed in Mumbai. The entrepreneur formally launched Naveli Ventures, the Nanda Family Offices venture arm, on October 6, 2026, to back deep-tech and frontier-technology startups.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin deep-tech founders in the US often struggle to raise from Indian capital; a serious Naveli Ventures becomes another bridge between Silicon Valley's Indian founders and Mumbai's family money.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cal AI's 19-Year-Old Founder Raises $10M for New AI Startup Persona
articles.excerpt: Zach Yadegari, whose calorie-tracking app was acquired by MyFitnessPal, raised $10 million led by Vine Ventures for Persona — an AI assistant starting in iMessage and moving to a $179 wristband.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's large contingent of tech founders and engineers, Persona is one to watch — a second act from a teenager who already built one of the fastest-growing consumer AI apps of the decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's New AI Note-Taking App Transcribes Meetings Entirely Offline
articles.excerpt: AI Edge Foresight, an experimental Mac app built on EmbeddingGemma 2 and Gemma 4, keeps all audio and files on-device — a privacy pitch aimed at confidential meetings.
articles.image_caption: Google's AI Edge Foresight app transcribes meetings entirely offline on Apple Silicon Macs, with no cloud subscription required. (Pictured: Googleplex headquarters in Mountain View.)
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's large contingent of tech workers handling confidential work, on-device transcription is a genuine privacy upgrade — but the app is experimental and English-first for now.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Deploys AI to Catch Ads That Secretly Funnel Users to Child Abuse Material
articles.excerpt: The company's new tools target "signposting" ads that look benign but route users to illegal material off-platform — and Meta says it actioned 5.3 million exploitation items in India this half-year.
articles.image_caption: A Meta logo displayed on a wall. The company said it actioned 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on Facebook and Instagram in the first half of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India accounts for roughly 16% of Meta's global child-exploitation takedowns, making this directly relevant to diaspora families whose children use Instagram and Facebook — and to relatives back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India to Release AI Regulation Consultation Paper Within a Month, Vaishnaw Says
articles.excerpt: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the consultation paper will cover AI safety, deepfakes, and the technology's psychological impact — with industry expected to carry the main burden of compliance.
articles.image_caption: Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. India will release its AI regulation consultation paper within a month, he said.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers, product leaders, and AI startups abroad will face new compliance duties for the Indian market, from content labeling to takedown timelines, once this consultation becomes law.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UPI Merchant Fee Rollout May Be Deferred to January 2027 Amid Retailer Pushback
articles.excerpt: Less than a week before the 0.40% UPI merchant fee was due to begin, retailers and fintech firms are pressing NPCI to delay it until January 2027 — and a decision is expected within days.
articles.image_caption: A UPI payment being made via a smartphone QR code scan. India may defer the proposed 0.40% merchant discount rate on UPI payments above ₹2,000 from October 15, 2026 to January 1, 2027 after pushback from retailer associations.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs using UPI during visits to India or through its international acceptance pay nothing under the framework, since the fee falls on Indian merchants — but the fight over who funds UPI’s next phase shapes the system’s sustainability as it goes global.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Targets One Billion 5G Users by 2030 as Scindia Opens IMC 2026
articles.excerpt: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia told the 10th India Mobile Congress that India has 550 million 5G users — the fastest adoption anywhere in the world — and set a goal of one billion by 2030, alongside a resolve to lead the world on 6G.
articles.image_caption: Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia addresses an audience at a podium. Scindia on Thursday set a target of one billion 5G users by 2030 while inaugurating the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: India's 5G and 6G push is a career and investment signal for the diaspora's large telecom and AI workforce, while Modi's anti-fraud framework push addresses the cross-border scam calls diaspora families receive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump to Award Top Science Medals to Musk, Nadella, Dell at Summit
articles.excerpt: The president will present the National Medals of Science and Technology and Innovation at Thursday's White House 'Science: A New Golden Age Summit' — the first time he has awarded either honor.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump embraces Elon Musk during a public appearance. Trump is set to award Musk the National Medal of Science at Thursday's White House summit.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, born in Hyderabad, will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation — a rare White House-level honor for an Indian-born tech leader.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ChatGPT's Teen Safety Guardrails Fail in Crisis, Independent Testing Finds
articles.excerpt: Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute ran more than 4,000 test prompts on teen accounts and rated ChatGPT for Teens an "unacceptable risk" for under-18s, urging OpenAI to restrict the chatbot to adults until its safeguards are independently verified.
articles.image_caption: A smartphone showing the ChatGPT app next to a laptop. Independent testing found the chatbot's teen safety guardrails failed in crisis scenarios.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families are among the heaviest adopters of AI tools for teens' schoolwork, so the finding that ChatGPT for Teens' parental alerts and study safeguards fail in practice is a direct, practical warning for parents — not abstract policy news.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Teaching AI to Act Drunk Makes It Leak Secrets, UNSW Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Three Indian-origin researchers showed that training or prompting five popular AI models to imitate drunken behavior made them far easier to jailbreak and more willing to disclose confidential information.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of a robot sitting at a bar counter with a wine bottle and a glass of amber liquid. UNSW researchers found that AI models prompted or trained to imitate drunken behavior become easier to jailbreak and more likely to leak information they were told to keep confidential.
articles.nri_angle: The research team — Anudeex Shetty, Aditya Joshi and Salil Kanhere — are Indian-origin researchers at UNSW whose work feeds directly into global AI safety practice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's Xreal Aura Ships at $1,279, Months Ahead of Meta's VR Glasses
articles.excerpt: Xreal's Android XR glasses, developed with Google, are on pre-order in the US at $1,279 and ship before the end of 2026 — undercutting Meta's $1,299.99 VR Glasses, which don't arrive until spring 2027.
articles.image_caption: The Xreal booth at Tokyo Game Show 2024. Xreal's Aura smart glasses, built on Android XR, are now shipping at ,279.
articles.nri_angle: Indian buyers get no launch date or pricing yet for either device, but Indian-origin engineers in the US are building both ecosystems and can buy the Aura this holiday season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Brings Gemini AI to Chrome on Android for Indian Users
articles.excerpt: The in-browser assistant summarises pages, answers questions about what’s on screen and connects with Google apps — while the new agentic Auto Browse feature arrives restricted to paid subscribers.
articles.image_caption: Google's headquarters in Mountain View, California. Google is bringing its Gemini AI assistant directly into Chrome on Android for users in India.
articles.nri_angle: Family in India gets the same AI-assisted browsing the US has had, and desktop’s eight Indian-language support means parents who prefer Hindi or Tamil can use it — relevant for diaspora households bridging the two.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gradiant Wins Five India Contracts as Chip Boom Turns on Water
articles.excerpt: The Boston water-technology company named a new India chief and will expand its Indian workforce by more than 40 percent as it supplies ultrapure water and zero-liquid-discharge systems to semiconductor, circuit-board and solar factories.
articles.image_caption: Precision equipment works on a semiconductor wafer during chip fabrication. Gradiant won five new contracts to supply ultrapure water and zero-liquid-discharge systems to chip, circuit-board and solar factories in India.
articles.nri_angle: Gradiant's expansion adds deep-tech engineering roles in India — including at its Coimbatore center that serves global projects — at the intersection of the country's chip ambitions and diaspora tech careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CDK Global Taps Indian-Origin Veteran Sudhakar Ramakrishna as CEO
articles.excerpt: Ramakrishna, former SolarWinds chief executive, succeeds Brian MacDonald at the Brookfield-owned automotive retail software company, taking charge on October 5 as CDK pushes its AI-driven dealership platform.
articles.image_caption: Sudhakar Ramakrishna, newly named president and CEO of CDK Global. He took charge on October 5, 2026, succeeding Brian MacDonald, and will lead the automotive retail software provider's AI-driven platform push.
articles.nri_angle: Ramakrishna's rise from a Kansas State computer-science master's to the CEO's office at a major U.S. software company adds another Indian-origin name to the top ranks of global enterprise technology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ElevenLabs to Invest Hundreds of Millions in India, Eyes Acquisitions
articles.excerpt: The $22 billion voice-AI company's India bet: local teams, Indian-language models, and possible acquisitions — with India already its biggest market by signups.
articles.image_caption: ElevenLabs, the AI voice company, plans to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in India, co-founder Mati Staniszewski told Reuters.
articles.nri_angle: India's voice-AI economy: $1M+ paid to Indian voice talent, 500+ Indian startups on free APIs, and an expanding India hiring push as a $22B global AI lab makes the country a core investment destination.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: QOSMIC's ARGUS Patent: Bengaluru Startup Wins US Patent for Laser-Communication Ground Station
articles.excerpt: QOSMIC Satellite Systems won a US patent on September 8 for ARGUS, a multi-aperture optical ground station for satellite laser communications — technology the startup says was conceived, engineered and validated in India.
articles.image_caption: An optical ground station telescope like QOSMIC's ARGUS, designed to receive laser communications from satellites
articles.nri_angle: QOSMIC's US patent is a signal for the diaspora that Bengaluru's deep-tech ecosystem is producing frontier space-communications IP — with NRI engineers, researchers and investors increasingly part of that loop as investors, collaborators and talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Engineer Builds AI App That Turns Potholes Into Accountable Complaints
articles.excerpt: Gaurav Sen's open-source Pothole Reporter matches dashcam-detected road damage to government contracts and drafts a ready-to-send complaint — photo, location, and tender reference — in about four seconds.
articles.image_caption: Commuters ride over a badly damaged, pothole-ridden road in Bengaluru. Engineer Gaurav Sen's open-source Pothole Reporter app detects such road damage and drafts evidence-backed complaints to civic authorities in about four seconds.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who drive Indian roads on visits home can use the free, open-source tool to file documented complaints, and its code is a replicable template for civic accountability anywhere.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIM Ahmedabad Gold Medallist Shubham Goyal Leads a 13-Member Team at Microsoft
articles.excerpt: The IIM-A graduate — Institute Rank 1 in his first year among 393 students, with the best overall GPA in the institute's MBA history — now leads a 13-member team at the software giant after patenting AI product work as a project lead.
articles.image_caption: A portrait photograph of Shubham Goyal. The IIM Ahmedabad gold medallist now leads a 13-member team at Microsoft, where he has served as project lead on patented AI work.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian professionals and students abroad, Goyal's rise is a concrete example of Indian-educated talent leading AI product work inside the world's largest software firms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Funds Deep-Tech Startups Lavishly but Rarely Buys From Them
articles.excerpt: Startups got less than 4 per cent of the Rs 5.03 lakh crore the government spent on GeM in FY26 — exposing the missing half of India's startup policy: public procurement.
articles.image_caption: An ISRO SSLV rocket lifts off. Defence and space procurement broke through only after the state changed how it buys, via iDEX and the SSLV transfer to HAL.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora engineers, founders and investors watching India from the US and Europe, procurement — not funding — is the variable that decides whether a deep-tech bet in India scales into a global company.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startup Funding Slips 8% in September Even as Big Deals Land
articles.excerpt: VC inflows hit $1.139 billion in September, down 8.3% from a year earlier but up 15.5% from August, as four $100-million-plus deals propped up the month, according to YourStory Research.
articles.image_caption: A photo illustration of a coin jar labeled VCs with coins flowing from a tap. Indian startups raised $1.139 billion in venture funding in September, down 8.3% from a year earlier, according to YourStory Research.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI founders and investors watching from the US, September's early-stage tilt — $557 million into young startups — is the signal that seed-stage India remains open for business even as late-stage capital stays selective.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI to Add Invisible Text Watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex in the EU
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's textGrain system subtly shapes word choices so detectors can spot AI-generated text, complying with the EU AI Act. API developers worldwide can opt in; the detector stays limited to approved researchers.
articles.image_caption: The ChatGPT app icon on a smartphone. OpenAI said it will add an invisible statistical watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the European Union over the coming weeks.
articles.nri_angle: No change for users outside the EU — watermarking is EU-only and opt-in on the API — but educators, employers and compliance teams should know these marks are invisible, fragile and often absent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: First Microblazar Found in Milky Way: Black Hole Jet Aimed at Earth
articles.excerpt: IRAS 18293−0941, a stellar-mass black hole 12,000 light-years away firing plasma at 75% light speed toward Earth, is the first confirmed microblazar — and a 100-times-more-powerful natural accelerator than the LHC.
articles.image_caption: Artist impression of microblazar IRAS 18293−0941, with one jet aimed almost at Earth (left) and the other striking a molecular cloud. The system, 12,000 light-years away, is the first confirmed microblazar in the Milky Way. Illustration: B. Marcote (JIVE/ASTRON).
articles.nri_angle: India's radio astronomers regularly join multi-observatory campaigns like this one, and the GMRT near Pune shares survey skies with MeerKAT, whose images confirmed the microblazar's counter-jet hotspot.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Demonstrates First Free-Space Quantum Link Over 5.56 km of Air
articles.excerpt: QNu Labs' overnight trial between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar transmitted secure encryption keys through open air with an error rate below 5%, laying the groundwork for satellite-based quantum communication.
articles.image_caption: Laboratory equipment for quantum key distribution research, including server racks, fibre-optic spools and monitoring displays. QNu Labs demonstrated Indias first free-space QKD link over 5.56 km of open air between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar on the night of Sept. 27-28.
articles.nri_angle: The quantum-encrypted systems that will eventually secure UPI payments and NRI remittances are being tested and owned domestically; the diaspora's financial links to India will rest on this indigenous stack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Indian Space Startups Ride SpaceX's Transporter-18 to Orbit
articles.excerpt: TakeMe2Space's MOI-1A, Dhruva Space's LEAP-2, SatLeo's TAPAS-1 and EON's MIRA imaging system all reached orbit aboard the October 1 rideshare from Vandenberg.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifts off on a Transporter rideshare mission. Four Indian space startups flew on the Transporter-18 mission.
articles.nri_angle: Indian space startups are selling heavily abroad — 80 percent of TakeMe2Space's customers are outside India, and French firm Sodern flew on Dhruva's platform — making the sector one of India's strongest diaspora-relevant tech exports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startups Raised $233 Million Last Week as Simple Energy's $180M Round Dominated
articles.excerpt: Sixteen Indian startups raised $233.6 million in the week of Sept 28–Oct 2, per Inc42's tracker — but Simple Energy's $180 million Series C alone made up three-quarters of it.
articles.image_caption: A stock illustration of a tablet displaying startup-themed doodles. Indian startups raised $233.6 million across 16 deals in the week of September 28–October 2, 2026, according to Inc42's weekly tracker.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors tracking India's startup ecosystem, growth-stage capital is flowing again — led by cleantech and EV — while early-stage founders face a tougher raise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Pauses Open-Source Bug Bounty Over Flood of AI-Generated 'Slop' Reports
articles.excerpt: Google stopped accepting new product vulnerability reports to its OSS VRP on October 1, saying a "significant rise in automated submissions" — mostly AI-generated and invalid — had overwhelmed maintainers.
articles.image_caption: The Googleplex in Mountain View. Google has paused its open-source bug bounty after a flood of AI-generated low-quality reports.
articles.nri_angle: India is one of the largest sources of independent security researchers; the freeze raises the bar for them — volume submissions are out, demonstrably real high-impact flaws are the only paying path left.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Android 17 QPR3 Beta 1 Arrives With 20-Plus Pixel Fixes
articles.excerpt: Google's first QPR3 beta targets Pixel 6a and newer, drops the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, and carries early code pointing to gamepad cursor control and phone-to-device unlock.
articles.image_caption: Image: @MishaalRahman via X
articles.nri_angle: The fixed eSIM self-disable bug is a genuine win for readers who toggle between a US line and a local eSIM while traveling; the beta's feature hints matter most to Pixel's enthusiast base, which includes many in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Global Factory Output Hits Four-Year High as AI Demand Lifts Manufacturing PMIs Worldwide
articles.excerpt: September PMI data shows the broadest industrial expansion since early 2022, led by euro zone factories and Asia's chip-exporting economies.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor fabrication plant. Global factory output hit a four-year high as AI demand lifted manufacturing
articles.nri_angle: The AI-driven factory expansion touches India's semiconductor and manufacturing ambitions as global chip and equipment demand accelerates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Extends ABN AMRO Tie-Up to Push Enterprise-Wide AI in Dutch Banking
articles.excerpt: The renewal brings Infosys Topaz's generative and agentic AI into ABN AMRO's core systems — announced a day after the stock hit a 52-week low.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys logo on a company sign. Infosys extended its strategic collaboration with ABN AMRO on September 30 to simplify the Dutch bank’s IT landscape and push enterprise-wide AI adoption.
articles.nri_angle: India's IT flagship is moving from AI pilots to enterprise-wide AI inside a major European bank even as the market punishes the stock (down 38% YTD) — a tension that defines the careers of millions of Indian tech professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Sends Four AI Chips Into Orbit as Project Suncatcher's First Test Takes Flight
articles.excerpt: A Planet-built prototype carrying four Trillium TPUs launched October 1 on SpaceX's Transporter-18 — the first step in Google's research into whether AI can run in space.
articles.image_caption: Google's illuminated logo. Google sent four Trillium TPUs aboard a Planet-built satellite on October 1 as the first hardware test of Project Suncatcher.
articles.nri_angle: India's own TakeMe2Space is launching an orbital computing satellite on a SpaceX rocket this year — the diaspora's space-tech ambitions are converging with Google's on the same orbital infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Will Restrict Free and AI Plus Users to Fewer Gemini Models From October 9
articles.excerpt: Free users lose Flash and Pro access; AI Plus loses Pro. But AI Pro subscribers at $19.99/month gain Deep Think reasoning — previously locked behind $99.99 Ultra plans.
articles.image_caption: Google's Mountain View headquarters. From October 9, free Gemini app users will be limited to the Flash-Lite model.
articles.nri_angle: The free-tier squeeze hits hardest for students and early-career developers — including India's large tech community — who rely on free AI tools for coding help and study.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Takes on Microsoft With ChatGPT's Own Office Suite at DevDay
articles.excerpt: At DevDay in San Francisco, OpenAI unveiled Space, Pages, and collaborative slides — workplace tools that put the ChatGPT maker in direct competition with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The company announced Space, Pages and collaborative slides inside ChatGPT at DevDay in San Francisco.
articles.nri_angle: For the large Indian diaspora workforce in American tech, the change is practical: documents and decks where distributed teams collaborate are becoming the place where AI agents operate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro Merges VLSI Design Subsidiary Into IT Services Arm
articles.excerpt: Wipro has merged its US chip-design subsidiary, formerly Eximius Design, into its IT services entity effective October 1, 2026, continuing its drive to simplify the group structure. There is no cash consideration and no change in shareholding.
articles.image_caption: Wipro has merged its VLSI design subsidiary Wipro VLSI Design Services into Wipro IT Services
articles.nri_angle: Wipro is NYSE-listed and widely held by Indian-American investors, and the absorbed unit traces back to a Silicon Valley semiconductor firm founded by an Indian immigrant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Expands Circular Centers to Give Retired Azure Servers New Life
articles.excerpt: Eight Circular Centers across three continents now securely decommission retired Azure hardware, hitting a 92% reuse and recycling rate as the AI buildout accelerates.
articles.image_caption: A data center aisle of server racks, in a Microsoft graphic about the Azure hardware lifecycle. Circular Centers process decommissioned servers and components from Microsoft's global fleet, reaching a 92% reuse and recycling rate last year.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cloud-infrastructure engineers staff much of the global Azure data-center workforce, and Indian enterprises on Azure gain verifiable hardware-reuse metrics for ESG reporting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 17, Navya Tuteja Built an AI Platform to Help Neurodivergent Job Seekers
articles.excerpt: The Thomas Jefferson High School senior wrote the algorithm for Raaha herself — and did it at a school where ChatGPT and Claude are blocked on the Wi-Fi.
articles.nri_angle: Navya Tuteja, an Indian-origin teen, is already lobbying state lawmakers and the US Department of Education on AI transparency — a sign of Indian-American youth moving from tech achievement into tech policymaking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IAF Signs Rs 135 Crore Deal With Delhi Startup for Mirage 2000 Simulators
articles.excerpt: Threye Interactive, a NewSpace Research subsidiary founded by former IAF Mirage pilot Sameer Joshi, will deliver VR-based part-task trainers for the fighter fleet after winning an iDEX challenge.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora technologists and investors, the deal shows India's iDEX pipeline producing bankable exits — a startup that began with a Mirage PC game now holds a real training contract with the IAF.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
